⚡ SAP Activate · Explore Phase · v1.1.0

SAP S/4HANA Cloud PE
Explore Phase Accelerator

Workshop accelerator for the Explore phase. Enriches BDCQ questions with country localisation and generates Cloud PE-compliant KDD logs — running locally on your laptop.

🧠 Claude AI engine
🔒 Local only — nothing stored externally
☁️ Cloud PE standards enforced
📊 Excel + PPT output
🌍 Country localisation built in
🎯
What this tool does
Two agents, one Explore-phase accelerator
AgentWhat it producesOutput
① BDCQ AgentTakes SAP's Business Driven Configuration Questionnaire and enriches every question with country localisation (GST, MTD, ZATCA…), industry context, and Cloud PE constraints. Mandatory statutory items are pre-answered so you walk into the workshop prepared.Enriched Excel BDCQ brief
③ KDD GeneratorTakes a list of SAP scope items and generates a Key Design Decisions log — Cloud PE-compliant design questions with options, RICEF/WRICEF classification, decision owner, and effort estimate.Excel KDD log + PowerPoint deck
Cloud PE onlyThe tool strictly enforces S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition standards. It will not produce on-premise or ECC concepts (ABAP, BAdI, SE16, SAP GUI). Everything is expressed through SAP Fiori apps and SAP BTP.

System requirements
What you need before installing
ItemRequirement
Operating systemWindows 10 or 11 (launchers are .bat files — Windows only)
BrowserGoogle Chrome (required for the SAP Deck Agent extension)
Disk space~1 MB for the zip; grows to ~70 MB after setup installs libraries locally
MemoryAny modern laptop — 2 GB free RAM is plenty
InternetRequired for: one-time setup (npm install), all Claude AI calls, and reaching SAP portals
AccountsAn Anthropic / Claude login and an active SAP for Me login
Network accessThe app listens on 127.0.0.1 only (your machine's loopback address). It is not reachable by anyone else on the network.

Prerequisites
Install these once, in this order — budget about 10 minutes
🟢
Node.js
Runs the local web app. Download the LTS version from nodejs.org and run the installer with default settings.
node --version
Should show v20.x or higher
🤖
Claude CLI
The AI engine. Nothing generates without it. Download from claude.ai/code and sign in with your Anthropic or Accenture SSO account.
claude --version
Should show a version number
🌐
Google Chrome
The SAP Deck Agent extension is Chrome-only. You also need an active SAP for Me login.
chrome://extensions
Where you load the extension
Verify firstConfirm both node --version and claude --version work in a new terminal window before proceeding. If either fails, redo that install step.
📦
Installation
Three steps, done once per machine
1
Unzip the tool
Copy the zip somewhere permanent — for example C:\Tools\ExploreAccelerator\. Right-click → Extract All.
Avoid sync foldersDo not extract to your Desktop or OneDrive — these sync folders can lock files while the app runs.
2
Run one-time setup
Double-click SETUP.bat. It downloads the app's dependencies (needs internet, about 1 minute). When you see "Setup complete. Run START.bat to launch." you're done.
If setup failsIf it reports "npm install failed" — Node.js isn't installed correctly. Redo the Node.js install, open a new terminal, confirm node --version works, then re-run SETUP.bat.
3
Install the Chrome extension
Unzip SAPDeckAgent-ChromeExtension.zip (inside the tool folder) into its own folder. Open Chrome → chrome://extensions → turn on Developer mode (top-right toggle) → click Load unpacked → select the unzipped folder. SAP Deck Agent should appear — pin it.
After any updateGo to chrome://extensions and click the ↻ reload icon on SAP Deck Agent. Chrome caches extension code — a reload is required for fixes to take effect.

Workflow A — BDCQ Enrichment
Turn SAP's raw questionnaire into a workshop-ready brief with localisation and industry intelligence
1
Get the BDCQ out of SAP — Chrome extension
In Chrome, open the SAP Roadmap Viewer → your project → Explore phase → Accelerators tab. Make sure the file list is visible. Click the SAP Deck Agent icon and click Scan for BDCQ Files.
SAP Roadmap Viewer — SAP for Me · Accelerators tab
The extension scans the Accelerators tab and finds all BDCQ Excel files — here it found 15 BDCQ files across 233 total files. The scan auto-scrolls the page, no manual scrolling needed. Once complete, click Save BDCQ Files and pick your project folder.
Scan frequencyPer project — re-scan the Roadmap Viewer for each new engagement. BDCQ files are client-specific.
2
Configure and enrich in the web app
Go to the BDCQ Agent page. Your questions will show as loaded. Fill in the configuration: client name, select BDCQ domains (with question counts per domain), set Industry and Countries in Scope for localisation.
SAP S/4HANA Cloud PE Explore Accelerator — BDCQ Agent · Configure tab
The BDCQ Agent Configure tab. (1) Source confirms your bdcq-questions.json is loaded — 15 domains, 1,414 questions. (2) Project Details for client name and output filename. (3) BDCQ Files — select which SAP domains to include; question counts shown per domain. (4) AI Enrichment Context — set Industry and Countries to control how Claude localises the answers.
Important distinctionThe domain selector controls which questions are included. Industry and Countries in the AI Enrichment Context section control how Claude enriches those answers — adding localisation context like India GST, UK MTD, Saudi Arabia ZATCA. They do not filter which questions appear.
Optionally paste scope item IDs from your DDA in the Scope Filter field and click Find Domains → to auto-select relevant BDCQ domains.
3
Generate and export
Click Generate & Edit for the full enriched output you can review on screen, or Quick Export ↓ to go straight to Excel. Output lands in the output\ folder and is downloadable from the Output Files page.
The enriched Excel will show country-specific rows tagged "Local – India", "Local – Saudi Arabia" etc. — statutory localisation questions generated from your country selection, each with a SAP Standard Value and Watch Out / Constraint column pre-filled.
⚙️
Workflow B — KDD Generation
Produce a Cloud PE-compliant Key Design Decisions log for a set of scope items
1
Load the scope catalog — Chrome extension (once per SAP release)
In Chrome, open SAP for Me → Process Navigator. Click the SAP Deck Agent icon and click Load Complete Process Data — KDD & Fit-to-Standard.
SAP Process Navigator — SAP for Me
The extension loads the full SAP catalog in one go — 657 processes (L3), 11 L1 domains, 22 L2 functions, 3,946 L4 steps. Builds both scope-catalog.json (for KDD) and scope-catalog-f2s.json (for Fit-to-Standard). Version shown: 2608. Click Save to Cartridge & Generate Agent Files and choose your project folder.
Refresh cadenceEvery 6 months — SAP releases in February (xx02) and August (xx08). The app warns you when your catalog is out of date. You do not need to redo this per project.
2
Select scope items and generate
Go to the KDD Generator page. Enter client name and project name. Select scope items by typing IDs in Quick Add (e.g. BD6, J59, BFB) or browse by LOB dropdown with text filter.
SAP S/4HANA Cloud PE Explore Accelerator — KDD Generator
The KDD Generator. Three sections: (1) Project Details — client and project name. (2) Select Scope Items — quick add by ID or browse by LOB with text filter, validated against all 657 SAP processes. (3) Selected Items — shows what will be generated. The Generate button shows estimated time (~40s for 3 scope items in parallel).
Click Generate KDDs with AI. The 5-agent pipeline runs: Cache → Library → Context → Generation → Validation. Live progress updates appear after each agent. Cache hits complete in under 5 seconds with no AI cost.
3
Quality check and export
A quality critique runs automatically after generation, flagging weak or non-compliant rows. Go to the KDD Editor to review, refine, and export.
Output files:
• output\Accenture_KDD_<Client>_<Project>_<Date>.xlsx — 5-sheet Excel (Cover · Instructions · Scope Overview · KDD Master Log · Summary)
• output\KDD_<Client>_<Project>_<Date>.pptx — PowerPoint deck

Workflow D — Gap Analysis
AI summary of where the client deviates from SAP standard

The KDD Analysis page runs an AI Gap Analysis (powered by Claude) across your decision set — a multi-step review that summarises where the client deviates from SAP standard and the associated WRICEF effort.

Use it to brief leadership on the shape and size of the gaps before detailed design begins. Three steps: local RAG scoring (instant, no AI) → Claude cross-scope integration risk analysis (~30–60s) → Claude gap themes and go-live health summary (~30–60s).

📁
Managing projects
Keep multiple client projects on one machine

Use the 📁 Projects panel in the KDD Editor to save the current KDD as a named project, load a different project to switch clients, or delete projects you no longer need. You will be warned if you have unsaved changes before switching — export or save first.

AI Suggestions memoryApproved decisions are retained across projects and power the editor's AI Suggestions on future engagements — the library grows with every project you run.

Security and data handling
This handles client data — treat it accordingly
TopicDetail
Local onlyThe app binds to 127.0.0.1:8321 (loopback). Nobody else on your network — office or client — can reach it.
What leaves your machineOnly the content needed for a given AI action is sent to Claude (via the CLI), exactly as any Claude Code session. Nothing is sent to any other server. The Chrome extension talks only to *.sap.com domains.
Where data livesYour BDCQ files, scope catalog, outputs, and saved decisions all sit in the tool folder on your disk — not in any cloud service the tool controls.
Accenture data classificationFollow your engagement's data-handling rules for anything you feed in and anything you export. When in doubt, check with your project lead.

Updating, uninstalling, and backups
Updating to a new version
1
Stop the app
Close the console window.
2
Back up your data
Copy output\, decisions\, and any saved projects somewhere safe.
3
Unzip the new build
Unzip into a fresh folder and copy bdcq\, scope-catalog.json, output\, and decisions\ across — or overwrite in place if instructed.
4
Re-run SETUP.bat and reload the extension
Run SETUP.bat (dependencies may have changed). In Chrome, go to chrome://extensions and click ↻ reload on SAP Deck Agent.
Your important dataYour non-regenerable files are output\ (everything exported) and decisions\ (KDD history and AI suggestion memory). Back these up periodically to your engagement document store.
⚠️
Known limitations
Limitation
Fit-to-Standard and Business Process Design agents are marked Coming Soon — not yet available.
The SAP Deck Agent extension is Chrome-only. The launchers (SETUP.bat / START.bat) are Windows-only.
Enrichment and KDD quality are only as complete as the source SAP data. If a domain is not broken out in the BDCQ, or a process lacks description in the catalog, the output reflects that gap.
AI generation needs internet and a working Claude login. Large scope sets can take a minute or two per step.
The tool targets Cloud Public Edition only — it deliberately will not produce on-premise or private-cloud concepts.

Troubleshooting
Click any error to see the fix
⚠️"Claude CLI not found" in the app▼
Claude is not installed or not on your PATH. Install from claude.ai/code, confirm claude --version works in a new terminal, then restart START.bat. Custom install location? Set an environment variable CLAUDE_PATH to the full path of claude.exe.
⚠️SETUP.bat says "npm install failed"▼
Node.js is missing or not on PATH. Install the LTS from nodejs.org, open a new terminal, confirm node --version, then re-run SETUP.bat.
⚠️Browser shows "can't reach this page" at localhost:8321▼
The console window is not running or is still starting. Start START.bat, wait for the banner, then refresh the browser.
⚠️"Port 8321 is already in use"▼
Another copy is already running — use that browser tab, or close the other console window and start again.
⚠️Extension: "Folder access expired"▼
Click Save BDCQ Files (or the save button) again — the extension re-opens the folder picker. Make sure you are on the current extension build.
⚠️Extension opens an SSO tab and the file doesn't save▼
Current builds wait for SSO and retry automatically. If it still stalls: let the accounts.sap.com tab finish loading (it closes itself), confirm you are logged into SAP, then click the save button again.
⚠️Extension finds no files▼
Turn on Developer mode in chrome://extensions. Be on the correct SAP page with the file list visible on screen. Scroll so files render. Click Scan Again.
⚠️Excel or PPT export fails▼
Ensure SETUP.bat completed (it installs the Excel/PPT builders). Do not delete the output\ folder.
⚠️"No WRICEF items" on export▼
Set WRICEF Type on your Gap rows in the KDD Editor first. Gap rows without a WRICEF type set will not appear in the inventory.
⚠️Generation is slow or times out▼
Large scope sets take time (60–105s per item in AI mode). Retry — partial results are cached. Cache hits complete in under 5 seconds.
⚠️Extension code changed but behaviour is the same▼
Reload it: chrome://extensions → ↻ on SAP Deck Agent. Chrome caches extension code and a reload is required for any fixes to take effect.
❓
FAQ
💬Does my client's data get uploaded anywhere?▼
The app runs locally and binds to loopback only. The single external call is to Claude (via the CLI) for AI generation — no other service receives your data.
💬Why do I need both Node.js and Claude CLI?▼
Node.js runs the local web app. Claude CLI is the AI engine the app calls. They do different jobs and are both required.
💬How big is the install?▼
The zip is under 1 MB. After SETUP.bat, the folder grows to ~70 MB on disk — that is the app's libraries (mostly the Excel/PPT engines), downloaded locally by npm. They are never transferred externally.
💬Can I work on more than one client at a time?▼
Yes — use the 📁 Projects panel in the editor to save and switch between client projects.
💬Do I need to re-scan SAP every time?▼
BDCQ: once per project. Scope catalog: once every 6 months (or when the app warns it is outdated).
💬Which browsers work?▼
The web app works in any modern browser. The SAP Deck Agent extension is Chrome-only.

Glossary
BDCQ
Business Driven Configuration Questionnaire — SAP's Explore-phase questionnaire that drives configuration decisions.
KDD
Key Design Decision — a documented design choice for a scope item, with options and rationale.
Scope item
A discrete SAP business process (e.g. BD6 — Vendor Invoice Management), identified by a short alphanumeric code.
RICEF / WRICEF
Reports, Interfaces, Conversions, Enhancements, Forms (W = Workflow) — classification of a gap or extension object.
Cloud PE
S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition — the standardised, Fiori/BTP-configured SAP deployment this tool targets. No custom ABAP.
LOB
Line of Business (Finance, Procurement, Sales, etc.) — how SAP scope items are grouped in the catalog.
Fit-to-Standard
The Explore-phase activity of mapping client requirements onto SAP standard processes.
MCP
Model Context Protocol — lets Claude CLI read the tool's data directly in interactive sessions.
DDA
Digital Discovery Assessment — SAP's tool for confirming which scope items are in play for a project.
L1 / L2 / L3 / L4
SAP process hierarchy levels. L1 = domain, L2 = function, L3 = scope item, L4 = individual process steps.
